Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Following up with a concise version of our needs so you can recommend Dedicated capacity options and give us a pricing ballpark. High-level:

- Production use for customer-facing LLM assistant (inference-only). Peak concurrency ~220 sessions, average session length ~120 tokens, 95th pct latency target < 400ms for 1-2 token responses and < 700ms for longer generations (up to 512 tokens).
- Models: planning to run a 70B decoder model and a smaller 13B reranker. We care about perf/$ and memory headroom for KV cache.
- Preference: private tenancy (dedicated pool), reserved monthly commit for predictable cost.

Questions:
1) Which GPU types should we prioritize? We’re comparing A100 40GB, H100 80GB, and L40S 48GB — tradeoffs on perf/$ and memory headroom would guide our commit.
2) What commit sizes (in GPUs) typically hit our latency SLO for this workload?
3) What discount tiers do you offer for 6- and 12-month reserved commits? Any flexibility on throughput guarantees for higher commits?

I attached our concise requirements doc. Can you share a short written recommendation + rough quote before we loop procurement? Prefer to keep the thread to the small group.

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins

Hi Sarah — great summary, thanks. I reviewed the attached requirements with Rishi (SE) and Vivek (sales lead). Quick answers up front, then a short recommended path and a provisional quote attached.

Short recommendation:
- Baseline: Start with an 8-GPU dedicated pool using H100 80GB for the 70B model inference (best perf and memory for KV cache). Add a 2-GPU pool of A100 40GB for the 13B reranker (cost-efficient).
- Commit: 8xH100 + 2xA100 reserved monthly commit for 12 months gives best perf/$ and predictable throughput. If you want to reduce cost, we can evaluate 12xL40S as a lower-cost alternative but you’ll need cross-shard routing and slightly higher batching to meet latency SLOs.
- SLA/throughput: For the 8xH100 pool we estimate sustained throughput to meet your 95th pct latency targets for single-turn requests at ~250 concurrent sessions with proper batching and KV cache warmers. We’ll provide an SLO page and can include an enhanced throughput guarantee at the enterprise tier.

Pricing highlights (provisional, see attached PDF):
- List price per GPU-hour (monthly reserved equivalent): H100 80GB = $X/hr (committed), A100 40GB = $Y/hr, L40S 48GB = $Z/hr.
- Discounting: standard 12-month reserved commit gets 18% off list; we can extend to 24% for deals >= $200k ARR committed.
- One-time setup + private control plane fee called out in the attached quote.

2) If the numbers look good, we’ll produce a formal quote (DocuSign) and a short mutual action plan for procurement.

Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU sizing and pricing — initial info request (technical note)

Hi Sarah — quick technical breakdown so you have concrete perf/$ and memory tradeoffs. I kept the math high-level; happy to walk through numbers on a call.

1) Memory considerations (KV cache + model weights):
- 70B decoder: depending on quantization and optimizer, you’ll need ~60–70GB of device memory for the model + ~10–20GB KV cache headroom for long sessions. H100 80GB avoids any offloading and gives comfortable headroom. A100 40GB requires tensor-splitting or model sharding (more complexity). L40S 48GB sits between but still tight for 70B without heavy quantization.

2) Perf/$ (rough normalized numbers; assume similar codegen and runtime):
- H100 80GB: baseline perf = 1.0, list cost = 1.6x (relative to A100 40GB). Perf per dollar = 1.0 / 1.6 = 0.625. Best for latency-critical, large models where memory headroom avoids extra batching penalties.
- A100 40GB: baseline perf = 0.7, list cost = 1.0x. Perf per dollar = 0.7 / 1.0 = 0.7. Good for smaller models or when model can be split efficiently; lower up-front cost.
- L40S 48GB: baseline perf = 0.85, list cost = 1.1x. Perf per dollar = 0.85 / 1.1 = 0.773. Attractive for medium-sized models and provides good perf/$ for batch-heavy workloads, but may require slightly higher batching to meet strict 95th pct SLOs for single-token latencies.

3) Operational complexity:
- H100: minimal engineering overhead for large models; fewer cache misses; lower variance in P95.
- A100: requires runtime sharding for 70B; increases complexity for fast failover and KV cache consistency.
- L40S: acceptable compromise; need to validate 70B memory fit with our quantized runtime.

4) Recommendation for FintechX:
- If your priority is meeting tight P95 latency and lowering operational risk: favor H100 for the 70B primary pool.
- If procurement wants the best sticker perf/$ while accepting some engineering work: A100 + additional GPUs could be used, but expect higher tail latency risk.
- If you want a balanced cost point: test 4xH100 + 6xL40S hybrid pool and use smart routing (70B on H100; shorter reranks and batch jobs on L40S). We can prototype with a 30-day proof-of-concept to measure real perf/$ and then finalize commit sizing.

Example sizing math (approx):
- 8xH100: estimated steady-state concurrency for 70B under your session profile = 200–260 concurrent sessions at target P95.
- 12xL40S (hybrid): similar aggregate throughput but higher variance; needs more total GPUs.

I attached a short capacity_matrix_fintechx.xlsx with the rough back-of-envelope numbers per GPU type. Happy to jump on a technical call Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_matrix_fintechx.xlsx (spreadsheet)
